mechanism: Both drugs possess anticholinergic and CNS depressant properties; oxycodone adds opioid-induced respiratory depression while oxybutynin increases anticholinergic burden, creating additive effects on CNS depression, constipation, and urinary retention.
action: Monitor closely for excessive CNS depression, respiratory depression, and severe constipation; consider alternative anticholinergic agents or opioid-sparing approaches; educate patient on fall risk and respiratory symptoms.
